identification: @vercel/vc-native-linux-x64: native Vercel CLI, Node.js Single Executable Application with pkg VFS
decisive_evidence: Fetched original preceding 65.2.0 with forager; its tarball SHA256 is f9409a884a45ae705bce101ab415fee80c5400fb19a7c9718577a00be87bab6c. Registry SHA512 integrity matches all three original tarballs.

The flagged embedded ELF is @esbuild/linux-x64 0.27.0, 11083960 bytes, SHA256 e4d41ef34045d7d1751c375cd4a90d07d929832f838830dc5212689a6567ee58. It is identical in 65.2.0, 65.3.0 and 65.3.1, and matches the independently fetched original esbuild npm release.

The keyring addon is unchanged in all three releases: 3126400 bytes, SHA256 817e0bf94d0e60786d7c2255601fe70ae0b7f684f8254ec124c3bb69a13f3f97, stored as @napi-rs/keyring-linux-x64-gnu/keyring.linux-x64-gnu.node.

65.3.0 vs 65.2.0 contains normal CLI changes: drains CRUD with user arguments and Vercel API requests, JS CLI fallback, framework diagnostics, builder/build-utils patch bumps, generated chunk renaming, and atomic native-cache writes. Node runtime executable code is unchanged; only 11 bytes differ before the SEA-note area. The entire Node .text section is byte-identical.

65.3.1 vs 65.3.0 changes exactly four VFS files: package/version metadata, the Brotli builder graph, and dist/commands/dev/index.js. The code refuses production proxy reuse/deletion and refuses a tunnel proxy as the first production deployment. The SEA bootstrap is identical.
The queue premise is not reproduced: 65.2.0 already fires the same suspicious vendor-check rule under the current unchanged rules. This is not newly introduced anti-VM behavior.
execution_paths: Rizin resolved esbuild entry to runtime.rt0_go. At VA 0x47e796 it queries CPUID leaf 0; VA 0x47e7a2 compares GenuineIntel words; VA 0x47e7ba sets a byte at 0xeb4322; non-Intel branches converge at 0x47e7c1 and initialization continues. Leaf 1 saves EAX at 0xeb43b0. runtime.init.1 at 0x410f20 consumes the vendor byte and feature bytes, setting bits in a runtime feature flag. No hypervisor leaf, hypervisor-bit test, payload gate or analysis-triggered exit exists in this matched path.

The engine carves the embedded Go ELF at an estimated 11081536 bytes, 2424 bytes short of its actual VFS entry. Parse failure and unavailable Go section metadata are carving/parser diagnostics, not evidence that the original executable is malformed or evasive. A complete VFS extraction identifies Go and parses normally.

SEA bootstrap mounts immutable VFS assets, patches module loading, and imports /snapshot/vercel-cli-binary-staging/pkg.js. That entry installs the native esbuild loader, handles explicit internal-eject or bounded snapshot script argv, then imports dist/vc.js.

native-esbuild.js materializes bundled esbuild into a content-addressed cache, writes/chmods mode 0755, and temporarily supplies ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH around module loading. pkg native-addon extraction writes SHA256-named cache entries for dlopen. New temp-file cleanup only removes its own failed cache-write temporary file.

Decoded the unpadded Base64 tunnel protobuf descriptor and Brotli builder graph. Connect/Dial and TCP data/open/close/window frames are developer-tunnel protocol data, not concealed executable stages. The client reserves a project tunnel through /v1/dev-tunnel, authenticates its gRPC stream with a client token, and forwards only the configured local target port. Cleanup releases its lease/proxy; 65.3.1 adds production safety checks.

Ordinary HTTP/DNS/TLS, crypto, subprocess execution, executable permissions, keyring/Secret Service, config credentials and telemetry support the documented deployment/build/authentication purpose. These supported dual-use observations remain detected. Bundling/minification, serialized protobuf descriptors and compressed builder data do not establish malicious obfuscation.
missing_context: No host execution history, installation authorization or operator session was supplied. The benign judgement rests on the recovered program and authentic release differences; it does not claim that every possible use of this CLI is authorized.

rule_changes.change: Same hex pattern and ELF/Linux/x86 scope; replace the Go exclusion with a baseline downgrade for recognized Go provenance. Go empty-program fixtures establish that this is ubiquitous runtime initialization; other contexts remain notable. Remove anti-VM mappings and preserve the CPU comparison observation.

Delete unsupported inference. Its required evidence is a vendor-word comparison and parse.error_count, neither of which establishes stripping or VM detection. Preserve the separate ELF diagnostic and CPU comparison.

Preserve matchers and scope; remove C2 ATT&CK mapping. The generic line does not prove documentation, so describe the union honestly as examples or escaped lines, notable. The engine filters this bare-any aggregator from scan output; its atoms remain visible.

Preserve matcher, severity and size/type/platform constraints; update every exact consumer. Ordinary Node WebStorage plus V8 does not establish Chromium or Electron. Remove WebStorage from Electron host identity and its strong two-marker composite; retain independent Chromium/Electron host and V8-marker combinations.
Add a generic generated protobuf header observation for source and native bundles; no Vercel-specific literal or runtime-activation claim.

consumer_and_coverage_audit: Searched exact IDs, directory selectors and existing fixtures before finalizing. No external exact consumer of the removed Intel composite/atom or moved HTTP-example IDs exists. Anti-VM ancestor selectors infer VM screening and must not regain ordinary CPU-vendor evidence.

Other instruction-density, hypervisor-bit/vendor, VirtualPC/VMware and Red Pill rules are retained. The existing x86 gate suite passed 11 cases; the existing native-source suite passed 9 cases, including hypervisor inventory versus timing-and-exit probes.

All exact Node WebStorage consumers were migrated with their existing suppression behavior. Electron-directory selectors now require actual Electron/Chromium evidence; adding Node to those exclusions would restore the unsupported product identity. Existing benign electron-runtime-ptrace-telemetry ELF retains the strong Chromium/Electron finding and zero suspicious/hostile traits.

Searched raw Intel-comparison bytes across available testdata and the named samples directory. External byte matches are PE/Mach-O files, outside the old ELF-only matcher. Corpus results are retained in scratch/vendor-comparison-corpus.json. No retained anti-VM positive is lost.

Focused inert controls cover ordinary and malformed Intel-dispatch ELF images, a vendor near miss, HTTP examples, generated-schema headers, Node/V8/WebStorage near miss, actual Chromium/Electron combinations, and executable-section-bounded hypervisor-bit probes. All 15 pass.

Attempted an encoded gRPC-service matcher while examining tunnel coverage; Cleave does not expose this binary protobuf descriptor as one decoded printable string. Retained the supported generated-header observation instead of claiming a forwarding or activation data flow from isolated schema text.

The first make validate exposed four does-nothing Go-runtime fixture failures for the newly retained notable CPU comparison. A compiler-context downgrade now retains the accurate comparison at baseline when .gopclntab identifies Go, rather than suppressing it as the original rule did. Ordinary non-Go/malformed contexts remain notable.

limitations: The model warns that its feature specification is v18 while the engine expects v21; a benign score is corroboration, not the behavioral judgement.
Cleave truncates the outer binary string view at 200000 strings; manual SEA extraction, decoded descriptor review and complete VFS diffs covered content beyond that view.
The retained notable ELF parse diagnostic concerns an automatically carved short Go image, not demonstrated evasion by the original package.
